paragraphs.english: Today, widespread social pressure to immediately go to college in conjunction with increasingly high expectations in a fast-moving world often causes students to completely overlook the possibility of taking a gap year. After all, if everyone you know is going to college in the fall, it seems silly to stay back a year, doesn’t it? And after going to school for 12 years, it doesn’t feel natural to spend a year doing something that isn’t academic.
paragraphs.chinese: 如今，要求学生立即上大学的普遍社会压力，再加上快速变化的世界中不断提高的期望，常常让学生完全忽视休学一年的可能性。毕竟，如果你认识的人秋天都去上大学，自己留下一年似乎很傻，不是吗？而且，上了十二年学后，花一年做些与学业无关的事，也让人觉得不太自然。

paragraphs.english: But while this may be true, it’s not a good enough reason to condemn gap years. There’s always a constant fear of falling behind everyone else on the socially perpetuated “race to the finish line,” whether that be toward graduate school, medical school or a lucrative career. But despite common misconceptions, a gap year does not hinder the success of academic pursuits — in fact, it probably enhances it.
paragraphs.chinese: 但即使这些感受确实存在，也不足以成为否定间隔年的理由。在社会不断强化的“冲向终点”的竞赛中，无论终点是研究生院、医学院还是一份收入丰厚的职业，人总是害怕落在别人后面。不过，与常见误解相反，间隔年并不会妨碍学业成功；事实上，它很可能还有促进作用。

paragraphs.english: Studies from the United States and Australia show that students who take a gap year are generally better prepared for and perform better in college than those who do not. Rather than pulling students back, a gap year pushes them ahead by preparing them for independence, new responsibilities and environmental changes — all things that first-year students often struggle with the most. Gap year experiences can lessen the blow when it comes to adjusting to college and being thrown into a brand new environment, making it easier to focus on academics and activities rather than acclimation blunders.
paragraphs.chinese: 美国和澳大利亚的研究表明，经历过间隔年的学生，通常比没有经历过的学生准备得更充分，在大学里的表现也更好。间隔年并非让学生退步，而是通过帮助他们为独立生活、新责任和环境变化做好准备，推动他们前进；这些恰恰常是大一新生最难应对的事情。当学生要适应大学、一下子进入全新环境时，间隔年的经历可以减轻冲击，让他们更容易专注于学业和活动，而不必为适应过程中的种种失误分心。

paragraphs.english: If you’re not convinced of the inherent value in taking a year off to explore interests, then consider its financial impact on future academic choices. According to the National Center for Education Statistics, nearly 80 percent of college students end up changing their majors at least once. This isn’t surprising, considering the basic mandatory high school curriculum leaves students with a poor understanding of the vast academic possibilities that await them in college. Many students find themselves listing one major on their college applications, but switching to another after taking college classes. It’s not necessarily a bad thing, but depending on the school, it can be costly to make up credits after switching too late in the game. At Boston College, for example, you would have to complete an extra year were you to switch to the nursing school from another department. Taking a gap year to figure things out initially can help prevent stress and save money later on.
paragraphs.chinese: 如果你仍不相信花一年探索兴趣本身有价值，那就想想它对将来学业选择的经济影响。美国国家教育统计中心的数据显示，近百分之八十的大学生最终至少换过一次专业。这并不奇怪，因为高中基础必修课程让学生对大学里等待着他们的大量学术选择了解不足。许多学生申请大学时填报一个专业，上了大学的课后却转去另一个专业。这未必是坏事，但依学校不同，太晚转专业后补修学分可能花费很高。比如，在波士顿学院，如果从其他院系转到护理学院，就得额外读一年。先用间隔年把方向想清楚，有助于日后减轻压力、节省费用。

sentenceNotes.sentence: Today, widespread social pressure to immediately go to college in conjunction with increasingly high expectations in a fast-moving world often causes students to completely overlook the possibility of taking a gap year.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: Widespread social pressure often causes students to overlook the possibility.
sentenceNotes.structure: to immediately go to college 修饰 pressure，说明压力内容；in conjunction with ... 表示与期望升高这一因素共同作用；causes students to overlook 为使役结构；of taking ... 修饰 possibility。
sentenceNotes.translation: 如今，立即上大学的普遍社会压力，加上快速变化的世界中不断提高的期望，常让学生完全忽略选择间隔年的可能。
sentenceNotes.tip: 找出主语核心 pressure 和谓语 causes，不要让中间的长修饰语遮住因果关系。

sentenceNotes.sentence: At Boston College, for example, you would have to complete an extra year were you to switch to the nursing school from another department.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: You would have to complete an extra year.
sentenceNotes.structure: were you to switch ... 是省略 if 的虚拟条件倒装，相当于 if you were to switch；would have to 表示在这一假设下必须做的事；At Boston College 限定实例。
sentenceNotes.translation: 例如，在波士顿学院，如果你从其他院系转入护理学院，就得再读一年。
sentenceNotes.tip: 看到 were + 主语 + to do，先还原为 if 条件句，再读主句结果。
